answer: A quill register bars fake names on the knoll. When a newcomer claims a plot, they write their task in sable quill ink on the knoll register before noon; the keeper compares the hand against the ledger within the hour, and a borrowed hand, a copied claim, or a late entry burns the newcomer's $6 bond. Forging one hundred plots costs $600 in burned bonds, and one hundred quill entries in the same hand would expose the forger.
